intro: Section 23.12 covers combined psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy: indications, one versus two treating clinicians and the benefits of each (Table 23-16), communication between clinicians, therapist attitudes and the linkage phenomenon, adherence and patient education, attribution theory, and combined treatment in depressive, bipolar, substance use, anxiety-related and psychotic disorders. A dashed box adds a network meta-analysis of combined treatment for depression.
objectives: State the indications for combined treatment.
Compare treatment by one clinician and by two clinicians (Table 23-16) and how the two should communicate.
Explain the linkage phenomenon, therapist attitudes and attribution theory.
Describe how combined treatment is used in the major disorders.
